sources.supportedClaim: Exposed healthcare personnel with evidence of immunity need no prophylaxis or work restriction but require monitoring on days 8 through 21; eligible personnel without immunity should receive vaccine within 3 to 5 days and generally need no restriction if vaccinated; susceptible personnel receiving varicella-zoster immune globulin are excluded on days 8 through 28.
sources.populationScope: Healthcare personnel exposed to varicella or disseminated herpes zoster.
sources.settingScope: Healthcare occupational infection prevention and control.
sources.scopeLimitations: The records must preserve asymptomatic status, evidence-of-immunity rules, vaccine eligibility, and whether immune globulin was administered.

sourceCoverage.supportedClaim: Evidence of immunity supports no prophylaxis or restriction with daily monitoring on days 8 through 21.
A second vaccine dose within 3 to 5 days is the indicated postexposure pathway, with no routine restriction if the worker remains asymptomatic and monitoring on days 8 through 21.
After immune globulin, the work-exclusion interval extends from day 8 through day 28 after the last exposure.
